Source: https://ankidraft.app

# [EN] Agent Editor (Alt+9) and A/B Testing Lab
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/agents-et-tests-ab/
Description: Build and version custom personas in Agent Editor (Alt+9), tailor Jinja2 prompts and model overrides, and compare models or pipelines side by side in A/B.

The **AI Lab** section in the sidebar brings together the **Agent Editor** (<kbd>Alt+9</kbd>), [DAG Pipelines](/en/cards/dag_et_rag/), and **A/B Tests** so you can tune how the AI drafts and audits cards for each subject.

## 1. Customizing Personas in Agent Editor (<kbd>Alt+9</kbd>)

Open **AI Lab › Agent Editor** (<kbd>Alt+9</kbd>) to create, organize in folders, and refine your agents:

- **Scope and Output Format**:
  - **Agent Scope / Usage**: `Forge Pipeline (DAG)`, `AI Consultant (MCP Server)`, or `Universal (Forge & MCP)` (filterable in the tree via **All**, **Pipeline**, **MCP**, **Universal**).
  - **Output Format**: `json`, `cloze`, `markdown`, or `text`.
- **Dedicated AI Engine (optional)**: pin a specific engine to the agent (for instance a fast or Vision-capable model), or keep inheritance enabled so it follows the **global default AI model** configured in **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>).
- **Jinja2 Instructions & Prompt**:
  - Start fast using **Templates...** (ready-made Cloze, Wozniak, or Language starter frameworks).
  - Insert runtime variables at cursor position (`{{ text_source }}`, `{{ last_output }}`, `{{ fields }}`, `{{ retrieved_chunks }}`, `{{ item }}`, `{{ initial_prompt }}`, `{{ state.variables.xxx }}`), browse **Variables**, and check the live interpolated prompt via **Preview**.
- **Tools & Role Presets**: select allowed tools manually or apply built-in presets (*Wozniak Auditor*, *Model & CSS Architect*, *SRS & Leech Analyst*, *RAG & Document Researcher*, *DB & Scripts Admin*, *Universal Consultant*).
- **Unit Testing & Version History**:
  - Click **Test** (<kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd>) to run the agent in isolation on a sample snippet before wiring it into a pipeline.
  - Open **History** (Time Machine) to inspect prompt revisions with visual diffs, or duplicate an existing agent before experimenting.

## 2. Comparing Configurations in A/B Tests

Open **AI Lab › A/B Tests** to evaluate two setups objectively on the same source document (or snippet) and target note type:

- **3 Comparison Modes**:
  1. **Compare two AI Engines** (for example `Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite` vs. a local Ollama or free OpenRouter model).
  2. **Compare two Prompts / Personas** using a shared engine.
  3. **Compare two DAG Pipelines** end to end.
- **Inference Controls**: keep shared Temperature and Max Tokens, or check **Independent A/B Settings** to vary parameters per branch, then click **Run A/B Test** (<kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd>).
- **4 Side-by-Side Inspection Views**:
  - **Visual Render** (interactive Front/Back preview with **Desktop 100%**, **Tablet 768px**, and **Mobile 375px** toggles plus **Sync Navigation A ↔ B**).
  - **Fields Table** (structured field-by-field breakdown).
  - **Raw JSON** (direct model payloads).
  - **Diff A↔B** (line-by-line comparison), paired with card counts, token totals, latency, and estimated USD cost per branch.

---

# [EN] MCP Server, External Agents & Workspaces
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/consultant_mcp/
Description: Connect Claude, Cursor, or Antigravity to AnkiDraft's local MCP server, sync your ~/ankiforge_agentique workspace, and review every batch in Safeguard.

AnkiDraft includes a built-in local **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** server (`127.0.0.1:8765`, automatically incrementing to a free port if occupied) so you can steer your collection directly from **Claude Desktop**, **Claude Code**, **Cursor**, **Windsurf**, or **Antigravity (`agy`)**, with **zero additional API keys**.

To provide your assistant with your active profile context and the live tool list, AnkiDraft also manages a dedicated **agent workspace** (`~/ankiforge_agentique` by default).

## 1. Inside MCP Server & Agents (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>)

The **MCP Server & Agents** view (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>) organizes everything across **5 sub-tabs**:

1. **Supervision & Configuration**: start, stop, restart, or ping the local server (Streamable HTTP and SSE transports), rotate the 256-bit Bearer access token (**Rotate token**), and copy ready-to-paste snippets for **Claude**, **Antigravity (agy)**, **Cursor**, or **cURL**.
2. **Safeguard & Validation**: mandatory two-phase human review gate. Individual proposals and multi-step **Staged Bundles** (locked until `commit_staged_bundle`) wait for your explicit approval (**Apply**, **Reject proposal**, **Reject all**).
3. **Tool Catalog**: searchable, domain-filtered inventory of all **93 MCP tools** exposed by the local server (cards, decks, tags, note types, albums, pipelines, agents, documents/knowledge gaps, and workspace drift checks).
4. **Activity**: live log of tool calls executed by your external assistant and their status.
5. **Guides & Workspaces**: manages your local agent workspace (`~/ankiforge_agentique` by default) with a compliance matrix, diff inspector, **Check Drift**, **Resync**, and **Initialize Workspace**.

## 2. The Agent Workspace (`~/ankiforge_agentique`)

Connecting the MCP server alone gives access to the 93 raw tools; **initializing and opening `~/ankiforge_agentique`** in Claude Code, Cursor, or Antigravity also equips your assistant with your active AnkiDraft profile state, safety rules, and synced tool catalog:

- **Root instruction files**: `AGENT.md` (master instructions), `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `README.md`, and `.gitignore`.
- **Profile & catalog files inside `.agents/`**:
  - `.agents/active-profile.md`: reflects the currently active AnkiDraft profile.
  - `.agents/mcp-catalog.md`: mirrors the exact list of MCP tools available on your server.
  - `.agents/glossary-and-internals.md` and `.agents/rules/ankiforge-conventions.md`: document AnkiDraft internals and two-phase safety constraints.
- **Synced skill templates**: `.agents/skills/general/` (`ask-forge`, `audit-ankiforge`, `code-review`, `domain-modeling`, `doubt-driven-development`, `implement`, `peewee-expert`, `pipeline-dag-ia`, `proposer-commits`, `rag-smart-coverage`, `research`, `tdd`, `ui-pyside6-design`) and `.agents/skills/meta/` (`gouvernance-skills`, `session-retrospective`).

:::note
When updating via **Guides & Workspaces › Resync** (or the `sync_agent_workspace` MCP tool), AnkiDraft runs a non-destructive 3-way sync on system files and **preserves 100%** of your protected user directories **`profiles/`** and **`_shared_models/`**, as well as symbolic links. Drift checks (**Check Drift** / `audit_workspace_drift`) are strictly read-only.
:::

## 3. Safety Safeguard: Two-Phase Human Validation

Neither an external MCP agent nor any tool can modify or delete cards behind your back:
1. The assistant stages proposed changes as intermediate patches or a sequential **Staged Bundle**.
2. Under **MCP Server & Agents** › **Safeguard & Validation**, you inspect a clear before/after diff of every added, edited, split, or deleted card.
3. Click **Apply** or **Reject proposal**: you remain in complete control of your collection.

## 4. Practical Step-by-Step Guides

- **[Zero API Key Workflow: Drive AnkiDraft from Claude or Cursor](/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/)**: quick setup and ready-to-use prompts for Claude, Cursor, or Antigravity.
- **[Anki Collection Rescue: Duplicates, Leeches, and MCP Hygiene](/en/workflows/sauvetage-et-hygiene-anki-mcp/)**: clean up an imported `.apkg` deck or `.colpkg` collection without losing review progress.

---

# [EN] Configuring AI Providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/
Description: Securely connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, OpenCode, or OpenRouter API keys and configure generation token limits, RAG settings, and MCP budgets.

AnkiDraft is **provider-agnostic**: you are free to use the AI service of your choice or switch models depending on the task.

## 1. Supported Providers and Gateways

In **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **AI Engines**, you can configure:

- **Dedicated Cloud API Keys (`CLOUD PROVIDER API KEYS`)**:
  - **OpenAI** (`GPT-4o`, `GPT-4o-mini`, `o3-mini`, `o1`, `o1-mini`)
  - **Anthropic** (`Claude 3.7 Sonnet`, `Claude 3.5 Sonnet`, `Claude 3.5 Haiku`)
  - **Google Gemini** (`Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite`, `Gemini 2.0 Flash`, `Gemini 1.5 Pro`)
  - **Groq** (`Llama 3.3 70B`, `DeepSeek-R1 70B` on LPU hardware)
  - **OpenCode** (`DeepSeek V4 Flash`, `Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite`, `GPT-5.4 Mini`, `Qwen 3.8 Flash`)
  - **OpenRouter** (`:free` models including `Qwen 3.8 27B`, `Gemma 4 31B`, `Nemotron 3.5 Lightning`, plus hundreds of paid models)
- **Configurable Local Servers & Gateways (`LOCAL SERVERS & ACCESS GATEWAYS`)**:
  - **Local Ollama** (`http://localhost:11434` by default) — see [Using a Free Local Model with Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/)
  - **OpenCode Gateway** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` by default)
  - **OpenRouter API** (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` by default)
- **Custom Models (`Add a model ▾` › `Custom model...`)**: register any model ID or OpenAI-compatible provider and configure its **Context Limit**, **Generation Cap (max tokens)**, **Default Temperature**, and capabilities (**Multimodal vision**, **Deep reasoning (Thinking / CoT)**, **JSON structured outputs**, **Free / included / local model**).

## 2. Getting a Free API Key (Student Guide)

| Free option | Credit card | How to obtain a key | Recommended preset in AnkiDraft | Caveats to keep in mind |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Google AI Studio** | No | Google account at [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com/) → *Create API key* (`AIzaSy...`) | `Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite` (vision + PDF) | Rate limits/min & /day; free-tier prompts may be reviewed to improve Google products |
| **OpenRouter (`:free`)** | No | Account at [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/) → *Keys* (`sk-or-...`) | `OpenRouter Gratuit (Qwen 3.8 27B)` | ~20 req/min & ~50 req/day (or 1,000/day after a one-time $10 credit top-up) |
| **Groq Console** | No | Account at [console.groq.com](https://console.groq.com/) → *API Keys* (`gsk_...`) | `Llama 3.3 70B` / `DeepSeek-R1 70B` | Strict tokens-per-minute caps on very long chapters |
| **GitHub / Campus / OpenCode** | No | **GitHub Student Pack** (`models.github.ai`), **OpenCode** gateway, or university endpoint | **Custom model…** / **OpenCode Gateway** | Depends on student verification or gateway limits |

**Activate it in 30 seconds inside AnkiDraft:**
1. Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **AI Engines**, paste the key next to the provider, and click **Test**.
2. Below the **ENGINES & MODELS CATALOG**, click **Add a model ▾** › **Popular quick presets** (for example `Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite` or `OpenRouter Gratuit (Qwen 3.8 27B)`), or open **Explore catalog & comparator...**.
3. Make sure **Free / included / local model** is checked in the model settings so the top-bar cost counter stays at `$0.00`.

:::note
For confidential medical notes or unlimited offline generation during exam season, prefer [local Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/) or your existing assistant via [MCP Server (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>)](/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/).
:::

## 3. API Key & MCP Server Security

- **Strict OS Keychain Storage**: API keys are stored in your **operating system's secure keychain** (service `AnkiForge`: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service). If no OS keyring is available, keys are never saved in plaintext on disk.
- **Direct Connection**: keys never pass through any middleman server—AnkiDraft connects directly from your computer to your chosen provider.
- **Automatic Log Redaction**: the async logging filter automatically masks secret keys (`sk-*`, `AIza*`) and `Bearer` tokens before writing logs to disk.
- **Local MCP Server (`LOCAL MCP SERVER`)**: in the same **AI Engines** tab, toggle the background server, adjust its **Listening port** (`8765` by default) under **Advanced MCP & diagnostics**, rotate the 256-bit Bearer token (**Rotate token**), and pick the default destination for contextual prompts.

## 4. Global AI Preferences, RAG & Token Caps

- **Global Default AI Model**: choose the default engine inherited by [Agents](/en/ai-setup/agents-et-tests-ab/) or pipeline steps when no override is set.
- **Global Feature Toggles**: control **Streaming responses**, **Vision capabilities enabled**, **Automatic card validation**, and **Automatic Linter audit**.
- **Generation Token Caps, CoT & Timeouts**:
  - Under **Advanced generation & RAG options**: adjust **Temperature**, **Max Tokens Cap** (`4,096` to `128,000`, default `16,384`), **Thinking Budget (CoT)** (`0` to `32,768` tokens), **Max generation timeout**, and semantic retrieval parameters (**RAG Chunks (Top-K)** from `1` to `20`, **Min similarity threshold** from `40%` to `95%`).
  - Under **DEFAULT GENERATION PARAMETERS**: set **Default temperature** (`0.30`), **Default max token budget** (`4,000`), and **Default request timeout** (`60 s`).
- **Consultant Budget Safeguard (`Consultant Token Budget` & `Consultant Cost Budget (USD)`)**: set dedicated caps for Consultant runs (up to `200,000 tokens` and `$5.00`, defaulting to `50,000 tokens` / `$0.50`), with a **preventive stop at 80% of the quota**.
- **Estimations & Spend Tracking**: document pickers and slice composers show an estimated token count (`~X tokens`) for your selected text, DAG pipeline steps accept per-step token budgets, **A/B Tests** estimate USD run cost, and the top-bar counter tracks cumulative consumption.

---

# [EN] Using a Free Local Model with Ollama
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/
Description: Generate atomic Anki flashcards 100% offline and for free on your computer using local Ollama models with automatic capability detection and zero API keys.

Prefer not to use paid cloud APIs, or studying confidential documents offline? AnkiDraft integrates natively with **Ollama**.

## 1. Install Ollama in 2 Minutes

1. Download and install Ollama from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com).
2. Open a terminal and pull a model suited to your computer's RAM:
   - **8 GB RAM**: `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` or `ollama pull qwen2.5:3b`
   - **16 GB+ RAM (e.g., Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4)**: `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` or `ollama pull mistral`

## 2. Connect and Scan Ollama in AnkiDraft

1. Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **AI Engines**.
2. Under **LOCAL SERVERS & ACCESS GATEWAYS**, locate **Local Ollama:** (`http://localhost:11434` by default; only local/loopback URLs are allowed as an anti-SSRF safeguard).
3. Click **Scan Models**: AnkiDraft queries Ollama (`/api/tags`), detects each model's capabilities automatically (Vision, Thinking/CoT, JSON output, context window), and imports new models into your catalog marked as **Free / included / local**.
4. You can also add or fine-tune a local model manually via **Add a model ▾** › **Popular quick presets** › **`Ollama Local (llama3)`** or **Custom model...** (useful to enable **Multimodal vision** or adjust **Context Limit** and **Default Temperature**).

:::tip
If local inference runs slowly on CPU or modest hardware, increase **Max generation timeout** and **Default request timeout** in **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **AI Engines** so long chapters do not time out prematurely.
:::

# [EN] Exporting Your Decks to Anki (.apkg)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/anki-sync/export-apkg/
Description: Generate a clean, ready-to-study .apkg deck for Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile with stable IDs and without losing your review history.

Once your flashcards are created and reviewed in AnkiDraft, transfer them to Anki in seconds using the `.apkg` exporter.

## 1. Exporting a Deck or Selection (.apkg)

1. Press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> (globally, outside **Note Types**) or click **Export Anki Cards (.apkg)** in **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>).
2. Pick a specific deck (including `Subject::Chapter` sub-decks) or **All Decks (Entire Collection)**.
3. Choose the scope (**All cards in deck** or **New cards only (`new` status)**) and keep checked as needed:
   - **Include all associated media (images and audio)**;
   - **Sync flags and suspensions as tags (`flag::color`, `is::suspended`)**.
4. Click **Export Package** to save the `.apkg` file.

:::tip[Native Flags & Suspended Cards in Anki Desktop]
AnkiDraft exports each note's stable GUID alongside native card flags and suspended status. To restore native flags and suspensions in Anki Desktop on import, check **"Import any scheduling information"** in Anki Desktop; otherwise `flag::...` and `is::suspended` tags remain immediately filterable.
:::

## 2. Updating Cards in Anki Without Overwriting FSRS / SM-2

AnkiDraft **never** injects FSRS or SM-2 review history/scheduling into `.apkg` files. Because each note retains a stable **GUID**, re-importing an updated `.apkg` into Anki Desktop refreshes card text and media **while leaving your existing FSRS / SM-2 review history and intervals intact inside Anki**.

## 3. Quick Multi-Format Export (JSON, JSONL, Text, Markdown)

Inside **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>), the **Export as Text or JSON (quick analysis)** button also exports your selection, active filter, or full collection to **`.json`**, **`.jsonl`**, **`.txt` (Anki TSV)**, or **`.md`**, as a single file or one file per card (with optional `id`, `guid`, and `chunk_id`).

---

# [EN] Importing a Deck (.apkg) or Collection (.colpkg)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/anki-sync/import-colpkg/
Description: Load your existing Anki .apkg or .colpkg decks into AnkiDraft to enrich notes, audit card quality, and track textbook coverage across chapters.

Already using Anki for months or years? You can bring your existing flashcards into AnkiDraft anytime.

## 1. Opening the Import Wizard (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd>)

Press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> (or click **Import Anki Package (.apkg)** in **Editor & Browser**) and drop your file: AnkiDraft supports **`.apkg`**, **`.colpkg`** (including Anki 23.10+ **Zstandard** `collection.anki21b` and `media.zstd`), as well as tab-separated **`.txt`** exports (with `#guid` column support).

## 2. `.apkg` / `.txt` vs. `.colpkg`

- **`.apkg` Package or `.txt` Export (Incremental Merge)**: choose whether to **Keep original deck hierarchy** or **Merge into target deck**. Unknown notes are added, while locally edited notes trigger [Smart Merge](/en/anki-sync/synchro_smart_merge/) on conflict.
- **`.colpkg` Collection Archive (`Full Anki Collection Replacement`)**: **atomically replaces** the entire *Anki Scope* (all decks, notes, note types, cards, and stats) with the incoming archive while **strictly preserving** your source documents, RAG chunks, AI agents, personas, and pipelines—and automatically creating a **SQLite backup** beforehand.

:::note[Anti-Zip-Bomb Size Safeguards]
By default, archive decompression is capped at **1 GiB** for `.apkg` packages and **5 GiB** for `.colpkg` collections.
:::

For a visual walkthrough of how AnkiDraft and Anki work together, read the [Visual Guide to the Distributed Lifecycle](/en/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/).

---

# [EN] Synchronization, Duplicates, and Smart Merge
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/anki-sync/synchro_smart_merge/
Description: Resolve conflicts during Anki imports with Smart Merge, preserve existing review schedules, and clean up duplicate flashcards automatically.

When collaborating on a shared deck or editing a flashcard in both Anki and AnkiDraft, **Smart Merge** protects your work.

## 1. When Smart Merge Triggers & 3-Pane Resolution

During an `.apkg` or `.txt` import, whenever an incoming note matches an existing **GUID** in AnkiDraft:
- **If the note has no local manual edits, merges, or version restores**: the incoming update is applied **silently** with no conflict prompt.
- **If content differs and the note has protected local edits**: **Smart Merge** opens with a **Similarity (%)** badge and **3 panes**:
  1. Left (red, read-only): **Local AnkiForge Base**;
  2. Center (blue, **editable**): **Merged Result (Interactive)** with per-field transfer arrows (`◀` / `▶`) and `Different` / `Identical` badges;
  3. Right (green, read-only): **Incoming Base (`.apkg`)**.

Built-in Smart Merge shortcuts: <kbd>Alt+Left</kbd> / <kbd>Alt+Right</kbd> (prev/next conflict), <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+Left</kbd> (**Keep All Local**), <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+Right</kbd> (**Keep All Incoming**), and <kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd> (**Confirm Merge**).

## 2. Duplicates, Merges, and Media Hygiene

- **Merges & Duplicates**: from **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>) › **Merges & Duplicates**, the quick scan in **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>), or your connected [MCP assistant](/en/ai-setup/consultant_mcp/), detect exact and near-duplicates (Levenshtein similarity) to merge redundant cards safely.
- **Media & Storage**: imported media files are MD5-deduplicated and Zstandard-decompressed when needed; orphaned media and TTS audio cache can be purged under **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **Storage**.

---

# [EN] Generating Flashcards with AI
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/ai-generation/
Description: Automatically turn textbook chapters and lecture notes into atomic Q&A or cloze flashcards with structured AI pipelines and human validation.

AnkiDraft helps you rapidly turn dense study chapters into atomic flashcards while keeping you in full control through human staging review.

## 1. Two Complementary Workspaces: Creation Studio vs. Batch Factory

AnkiDraft separates **interactive card crafting** (one excerpt or free-form note) from **batch production** (an entire book split into queued jobs):

### Option A — Creation Studio (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>): Focused & Interactive
Best for working closely on **one section**, **a pasted excerpt**, or a **New Input** (<kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd>):
1. Open **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>).
2. Pick a document section on the left (with its scope) or click **New Input** (<kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd>).
3. Under **Anki Targets** and **AI Orchestration**, select the deck, note type, **AI Engine**, and **Agent Pipeline**; optionally enable **Multimodal Vision** (`ON`/`OFF` badge based on engine capability) and **Advanced Settings** (*Temperature*, *Max Tokens*), then press <kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd>.
4. Review cards with live preview (<kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>V</kbd> to approve, <kbd>Delete</kbd> / <kbd>Backspace</kbd> / <kbd>R</kbd> to reject, <kbd>E</kbd> to edit, <kbd>Alt+Left</kbd> / <kbd>Alt+Right</kbd> to navigate, or **Accept All** in 1 click), then press <kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd> to save.

### Option B — Batch Factory (<kbd>Alt+6</kbd>): Multi-Chapter Queue Processing
Best for processing **multiple chapters or whole textbooks** through a resumable queue:
1. Open **Batch Factory** (<kbd>Alt+6</kbd>).
2. Click **Compose Batch…** (<kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd>) to slice your sources ([Scope & Chapters](/en/sources/scope-and-slices/)):
   - **Direct Mode**: each checked section creates one generation task.
   - **Automatic Mode**: groups or splits sections automatically by length.
3. Configure targets and toggles (**Vision (PDF)**, **Auto Validation**, **Full Document by Chunks**, *Advanced Settings*), then launch the queue (<kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd>). If a single task fails, use **Resume Batch** without restarting from scratch.
4. Review generated cards in the bottom **Review** tab (<kbd>Alt+Up</kbd> / <kbd>Alt+Down</kbd> to switch slices) before saving to your collection.

## 2. Tailoring AI Behavior (Agents & Pipelines)

Extraction style is driven by the **Agent Pipeline** chosen in Studio or Batch Factory and customized in **Agent Editor** (<kbd>Alt+9</kbd>). AnkiDraft includes built-in presets ready to clone and refine:
- **Wozniak Atomic Generator** and **Auto-Cloze Generator** (focused cloze cards);
- **Medical & Anatomy Specialist** (mechanisms, clinical concepts, anatomical relations);
- **Scientific Formulas & KaTeX** (derivations and mathematical notation);
- **Languages & Vocabulary Tutor** (contextual examples, idioms, pronunciation);
- **Law, Standards & Case Law** (core concepts, distinctions, rulings).

:::tip[Per-Note-Type AI Instructions]
You can also define an **AI Role** (or structured table via **Prompt for AI**) directly on any note type under **Note Types** (<kbd>Alt+8</kbd>) to guide how AI populates each field.
:::

## 3. Human Review Before Saving (Staging)

No AI-generated card is ever added blindly to your collection: all proposals land in the review queue (**Studio** or Batch Factory's **Review** tab) where you can accept, edit, or reject each card before saving (<kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd>).

---

# [EN] Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Audio Cards
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/audio-tts/
Description: Automatically generate natural offline audio pronunciation for language and terminology flashcards using Kokoro or Piper neural TTS voices locally.

When studying foreign languages, medical terminology, or music, attaching an audio clip to a flashcard dramatically boosts retention.

## 1. Install Offline TTS Engines and Voices

Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **Audio & TTS** before generating offline audio for the first time:

- **Piper TTS (local & fast)**: expand **MOTEUR LOCAL PIPER**, click **Download Piper CLI (1-Click)**, then select and download one or more target-language voice packs under **Additional Voices** (French, English, Japanese, Spanish, German, etc.).
- **Kokoro-82M (optional high-fidelity local engine)**: expand **MOTEUR LOCAL KOKORO-82M (OPTIONNEL)** and click **Install Kokoro (1-Click)** to download the local runner and ONNX model files.
- **Zero-download options**: **Edge-TTS** works directly over an internet connection (free, no API key), and the **OS System Engine** uses native voices already installed on your computer.

Click **Test Selected Voice** to verify playback before running a batch job.

## 2. Generating and Playing Field Pronunciation in One Click

1. In **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>), open a note and click the **Generate Audio Pronunciation (TTS)** speaker icon in the target field's header. If text is highlighted, only the selection is synthesized; otherwise the full field is read (with Cloze tags `{{c1::word}}` cleanly expanded first).
2. Audio is synthesized using the engine and voice configured in **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **Audio & TTS**, cached in your media folder, and appended as an Anki sound tag ready for Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile:
   - **Edge-TTS**: generates an **`.mp3`** file (`[sound:tts_xxx.mp3]`);
   - **Piper TTS** and **Kokoro-82M**: generate a **`.wav`** file (`[sound:tts_xxx.wav]`);
   - **OS System Engine**: generates a **`.wav`** file (or **`.m4a`** on macOS).
3. Whenever a field contains a `[sound:...]` tag, a **Play / Stop** button appears in its header for instant playback.

## 3. Batch Audio Generation via a DAG Pipeline

To attach audio automatically across a batch of newly generated cards, add an **`Audio Generation (TTS)`** (`AUDIO_TTS`) step at the end of your workflow in **Pipelines** (see [Generation Pipelines](/en/cards/dag_et_rag/)). You can configure the source field, target field (append or replace), TTS engine, and voice.

---

# [EN] Generation Pipelines and Smart Coverage
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/dag_et_rag/
Description: Automate multi-step flashcard creation with DAG pipelines and fill knowledge gaps across your textbooks using local RAG and Smart Coverage tools.

For large textbooks and courses, AnkiDraft combines the **DAG Pipelines** editor (directed acyclic workflows) and **Smart Coverage** (local RAG & alignment).

## 1. Chaining Up to 6 Step Types in a DAG Pipeline

In the **Pipelines** view, each workflow chains reusable, inspectable steps with cycle safeguards and conditional jumps (`↳ step`):
- **`RAG_RETRIEVAL` (Vector RAG Search)**: fetches top matching chunks (`top_k`) from an indexed course.
- **`LLM_PROMPT` (AI Agent)**: generates or audits flashcards with an agent (plus optional **per-step prompt override** without altering the global agent).
- **`MAP_REDUCE` (Parallel Batch Generation)**: splits and processes dense documents in parallel batches.
- **`HUMAN_VALIDATION` (Copilot Pause)**: pauses execution so you can approve or refine an intermediate outline before card generation.
- **`PYTHON_TOOL` (Deterministic Python Tool)**: runs non-LLM transforms (e.g., `clean_html_latex`, `validate_json_schema`, `deduplicate_cards_levenshtein`).
- **`AUDIO_TTS` (TTS Audio Generation)**: automatically attaches `[sound:...]` pronunciation tags to generated cards.

Three ready-to-use templates (*Standard Course Pipeline*, *Copilot Pipeline with Human Validation*, *High-Precision Map-Reduce & RAG*) are available under **Preset Templates…**, with **step-by-step simulation** (<kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd>) and JSON or cross-profile import/export.

## 2. Spotting Uncovered Chapters (Smart Coverage)

Using local semantic indexing and provenance links (`NoteChunkLinkModel`), AnkiDraft compares your existing flashcards against your entire course:
- In **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>) › **Coverage** or **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>) › **Documents**, it highlights orphan sections that have zero flashcards yet.
- Click **Forge Section** (or <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+F</kbd>) to generate only the missing cards without duplicating concepts you already covered.

---

# [EN] Note Editor, KaTeX Math, and Cloze Deletions
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/editeur_notes_katex/
Description: Write and format Anki flashcards with live KaTeX math preview, cloze deletions, rich media attachments, and full per-note revision history in AnkiDraft.

The **Editor & Browser** view (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>) combines deck browsing and full note editing with live Anki card preview (<kbd>Ctrl+P</kbd> to toggle preview, <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+T</kbd> to switch between **📝 Notes** and **🗂️ Cards**).

## 1. Writing Math and Chemistry Formulas (KaTeX)

AnkiDraft renders your LaTeX equations live without waiting for an Anki export:
- **Quick insert**: click the **KaTeX Formula** toolbar icon or press <kbd>Ctrl+M</kbd>.
- **Inline formula**: wrap your expression in `\( ... \)` or `$ ... $` (e.g., `$E = mc^2$`).
- **Centered block formula**: use `\[ ... \]` or `$$ ... $$`.
- **LaTeX Autocompletion**: type `\` followed by the first letters of a symbol (`\alpha`, `\frac`, `\sum`) to open the completion popup.

## 2. Cloze Deletions, Media, and Customizable Toolbar

Cloze cards are ideal for memorizing precise definitions or key terms:
1. Highlight the word or phrase you want to hide.
2. Click **Cloze** or press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd> to insert the next index `{{c1::your text}}` (or with a hint `{{c1::answer::hint}}`).
3. The toolbar also includes HTML formatting, code blocks, links (<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>), image insertion (plus drag-and-drop directly into any field), and toolbar customization via `...`.
4. Each field header provides a **TTS** speaker button for audio pronunciation, and course-linked notes display **View Course ➔** to jump straight back to the source passage.

:::tip[Interactive Diagrams and Charts]
To mask labels directly on anatomy plates or technical diagrams, use [Smart Image Occlusion (Vision AI)](/en/cards/image-occlusion/).
:::

## 3. Group Editing, Flags, and Bulk Actions

- **Atomic Group Edit** (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+E</kbd>) & **Targeted Find / Replace** (<kbd>Ctrl+Alt+F</kbd>): add/remove tags (while preserving `source:`, `section:`, `page:` provenance tags) or edit a field across selected notes (*Replace*, *Append*, *Prepend*, *Find and replace*).
- **Fast organization & AI bulk tools**: apply flags (<kbd>Ctrl+0</kbd> to <kbd>Ctrl+7</kbd>), suspend/unsuspend (<kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> or <kbd>!</kbd>), move decks (<kbd>Ctrl+D</kbd>), change note type (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+M</kbd>), clean up tags (**Tag Hygiene & Merge…**), or run **AI Batch Edit** / **Auto-Tagging** on a selection.

## 4. Revision History (Time Machine)

Edited a card by mistake? Every save (<kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd>) stores a local snapshot in the note history: click **History** or press <kbd>Ctrl+H</kbd> to open the **Time Machine**, compare snapshots, and restore previous wording in one click.

---

# [EN] Smart Image Occlusion (Vision AI)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/image-occlusion/
Description: Create Image Occlusion Enhanced flashcards from anatomy or course diagrams using manual masks, Vision AI label detection, and Hide All or Hide One.

**Smart Image Occlusion** (`Image Occlusion AI`) turns anatomy plates, maps, flowcharts, and scientific diagrams into visual flashcards using the **`Image Occlusion Enhanced`** standard directly inside AnkiDraft.

## 1. Opening a Diagram in the Occlusion Studio

Several direct entry points feed into the occlusion canvas:
- From **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>) › **Figures** tab on an imported PDF: launch image occlusion in one click on any extracted diagram.
- From an **Image Album**: open any scanned plate directly in the occlusion tool ([Image Albums](/en/sources/albums-images/)).
- Inside the occlusion dialog: click **Change Image…** (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.bmp`, `.svg`) or **Paste Image** straight from your clipboard.

## 2. Manual Masking or Vision AI Auto-Detection

1. **Detect with AI**: automatically scans the diagram with a Vision-capable model to place occlusion boxes over labels and fill the **Masks & Labels** table.
2. **Manual Draw & Adjust**: switch between **Select / Move Mode** and **Draw Mode** to sketch, resize, or delete (<kbd>Delete</kbd>) mask rectangles freely.
3. Refine **`Text / Answer`** and **`Hint`** entries in the right-hand table and use the zoom controls as needed.

:::note[Vision AI Requirement]
Automatic label detection requires a **Vision-capable AI engine** (Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic API or local multimodal Ollama model) configured in **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>). Manual mask drawing works 100% offline with zero API keys.
:::

## 3. Occlusion Modes and Note Generation

Before generating notes into your chosen **Target Deck** (with an optional card header and comma-separated tags such as `image-occlusion`), pick your study mode:
- **`Hide All, Reveal One (Hide All)`**: best when neighboring labels would otherwise give away the answer. Keep **`Keep other masks hidden on back`** checked to prevent contextual leaks while reviewing.
- **`Hide One, Reveal One (Hide One)`**: keeps surrounding labels visible when spatial context helps anchor a specific term.

On first use, AnkiDraft automatically provisions the **`Image Occlusion Enhanced`** note type in your collection, ready for `.apkg` export to Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile.

# [EN] Quality Audit and Wozniak's 20 Rules
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/linter_wozniak/
Description: Detect and split overloaded, vague, or hard-to-remember flashcards with the Wozniak 20-Rules Linter to boost long-term Anki retention daily.

A poorly formulated flashcard (too long, testing multiple facts at once, or lacking context) quickly turns into a "leech" that you repeatedly fail in Anki.

AnkiDraft includes a built-in **Pedagogical Linter** based on **Piotr Wozniak's 20 rules of formulating knowledge** (creator of SuperMemo).

## 1. Wozniak Audit in Analysis & AI Audit (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>)

Open **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>) › **Wozniak Audit & Linter**, pick a deck, and run the audit (<kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd>). AnkiDraft scores the deck out of 100 across **4 weighted categories** (with customizable settings under **Rules**):
- **Atomicity & Restructuring**: overloaded answers or cards testing multiple independent facts.
- **Cloze & Unambiguity**: vague prompts or overly broad clozes (plus a dedicated toggle to keep or convert clozes into Q&A).
- **Disambiguation & Context**: interfering cards that look too similar during recall.
- **KaTeX Formulas & Clarity**: ambiguous or malformed math expressions.

A quick linter dialog can also be launched directly on selected notes inside **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>).

## 2. Splitting Leeches and Merging Duplicates

- **Split into Atomic Cards**: under **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>) › **Tokens & SRS** › **Leech Cards Diagnostic**, locate high-lapse cards and click **Split** to generate and apply (via *Two-Phase Commit* preview) a breakdown into 2 or 3 atomic cards.
- **Duplicate Detection & Merge**: the **Merges & Duplicates** tab (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>, as well as the quick duplicate scan in `Editor & Browser`) clusters near-identical notes using Levenshtein similarity so you can merge redundant cards safely without losing review history.

---

# [EN] Note Types, Templates, and CSS Styling
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/note-types-and-templates/
Description: Customize note types, HTML/Mustache card templates, AI Role guides, LaTeX headers, CSS snippets, and light/dark styling for Anki Desktop and Web.

The **Note Types** view (<kbd>Alt+8</kbd>) lets you design, style, preview, and share note types that remain 100% compatible with the Anki ecosystem.

## 1. Initial Model, Starter Pack, and Image Occlusion

- **Clean initial profile**: a blank AnkiDraft profile ships only with a single **`Basic` (`Basique`)** note type (`Front`/`Back` or `Recto`/`Verso`) so your first `.apkg` import never collides with pre-seeded templates.
- **On-demand Starter Pack**: open **Starter Pack** inside **Note Types** (<kbd>Alt+8</kbd>) to install **`Cloze Deletion`** (`{{cloze:Text}}`) and additional ready-made community models.
- **`Image Occlusion Enhanced`**: provisioned automatically the first time you open [Smart Image Occlusion](/en/cards/image-occlusion/).

## 2. HTML/Mustache Templates, CSS, LaTeX, and Snippets

Every note type features **4 sub-tabs** (*CSS Style*, *Front HTML*, *Back HTML*, and **LaTeX** preamble/footer for compilation) alongside a live preview (**light / dark mode** toggle using automatic sample values or a real witness note):
- Use standard **Anki Mustache** syntax (`{{Front}}`, `{{FrontSide}}`, `{{cloze:Text}}`) and the **Insertion Helpers** drawer (fields, cloze, CSS classes, structure).
- Browse the **Snippets** library (*Info*, *Warning*, *Error*, *Tip*, *Theorem* callouts, difficulty/exam badges, MCQ grids, code blocks, KaTeX boxes) with automatic CSS conflict detection.
- Fill in **AI Role** (or the structured **Prompt for AI** table) to tell AI agents exactly how each field should be populated during generation.

## 3. Import, Export, and Smart Reconciliation

- Import or export note types as `.afmodel` / `.json` (<kbd>Ctrl+Alt+O</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd>), or import a model directly from another AnkiDraft profile.
- When importing an `.apkg` deck whose note type already exists in your collection, AnkiDraft reconciles it cleanly instead of creating duplicate `Basic-12345` models.

# [EN] Installing AnkiDraft
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/installation/
Description: Download, install, and update AnkiDraft on macOS, Windows, and Linux from the latest official GitHub release with Ed25519 signature verification.

AnkiDraft is a standalone desktop application. You do not need to install Python or any developer tools on your computer.

## 1. Download the Installer (Latest Release)

Visit the [AnkiDraft homepage](https://ankidraft.app/en/#download) or go straight to the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/releases/latest) to automatically fetch the package for your system:

| Operating System | Published Formats (`releases/latest`) | System Requirements |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **macOS** | Disk image `.dmg` (Apple Silicon) or `.zip` archive | macOS 13 (Ventura) or newer, Apple Silicon chip (M1/M2/M3/M4) |
| **Windows** | Standalone `.exe` installer or portable `.zip` archive | Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit) |
| **Linux** | Portable `.AppImage` executable or `.tar.gz` archive | Modern 64-bit Linux distribution (Ubuntu 22.04+, Fedora, Arch) |

## 2. Step-by-Step Setup

### On macOS
1. Double-click the `.dmg` disk image downloaded from the [latest release](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/releases/latest).
2. Drag the application icon into your **Applications** folder.
3. **First launch:** official macOS releases are notarized by Apple; if you install a nightly or unsigned build and macOS shows a Gatekeeper warning:
   - Open **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security**, scroll to **Security**, and click **Open Anyway** for AnkiDraft (or **Right-click** → **Open** on the app in Applications).
   - You only need to do this **once** for that installation.

### On Windows *(not yet tested in production)*
1. If you download the `.exe` installer, double-click it and follow the wizard (no administrator rights required for a user-level installation).
2. If you download the portable `.zip` archive, extract it and run the main executable.

### On Linux (AppImage) *(not yet tested in production)*
1. Make the downloaded `.AppImage` file executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x *.AppImage
   ```
2. Launch the application by double-clicking it or executing it in your terminal.

## 3. Where Is Your Data Stored?

All your study data stays locally on your drive inside your user folder:
- **macOS:** `/Users/<your-name>/.ankidraft/profiles/<profile_name>/`
- **Windows:** `C:\Users\<YourName>\.ankidraft\profiles\<profile_name>\`
- **Linux:** `/home/<your-name>/.ankidraft/profiles/<profile_name>/`

Each profile contains:
- `ankidraft.db`: your local SQLite database of cards, documents, and history.
- `media/`: images and audio clips attached to your flashcards.
- `backups/`: automatic local snapshots (up to 5 recent backups kept on startup and before sensitive operations).
- `staging/`: isolated temporary workspace for staged transfers and MCP file staging.

## 4. Automatic Updates

AnkiDraft automatically checks for official releases and verifies both the SHA-256 manifest (`checksums.txt`) and its Ed25519 cryptographic signature (`checksums.txt.sig`) when provided.

## 5. Report an Issue or Suggest Improvements

If you run into a bug, if your operating system is not yet available, or if you have ideas for improvements, please open an issue on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/issues).

---

# [EN] Interface Overview
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/interface-overview/
Description: Take a guided tour of AnkiDraft workspaces, 4 switchable window layouts (IDE, macOS, Dashboard, Glass), and 12 built-in visual themes for study.

AnkiDraft is designed to stay clean and responsive whether you work on a laptop screen or an ultrawide monitor.

## 1. Main Workspaces

The sidebar organizes **11 workspaces** into 4 sections:

### General
- **Dashboard** (<kbd>Alt+1</kbd>): overview of your decks, document coverage progress, and recent activity ([Import .apkg / .colpkg](/en/anki-sync/import-colpkg/) · [Export .apkg](/en/anki-sync/export-apkg/)).

### Forge & Tools
- **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>): interactive, focused card crafting from an excerpt or free-form input (<kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd>) with live preview and card-by-card review ([AI Generation](/en/cards/ai-generation/)).
- **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>): manual creation, editing with live KaTeX math preview, cloze deletions, per-field TTS, and card management ([Note Editor & KaTeX](/en/cards/editeur_notes_katex/)).
- **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>): detection of overloaded, vague, or hard-to-memorize flashcards and coverage tracking ([Wozniak Linter](/en/cards/linter_wozniak/)).
- **MCP Server & Agents** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>): connect external agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity) to your local collection via MCP with Safeguard review ([MCP Server & Agents](/en/ai-setup/consultant_mcp/)).
- **Batch Factory** (<kbd>Alt+6</kbd>): batch production queue for whole books or multiple chapters (*Batch Slice Composer* with <kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd>, resumable jobs, and Staging review) ([AI Generation](/en/cards/ai-generation/) · [Scope & Slices](/en/sources/scope-and-slices/)).

### Library
- **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>): library of your PDFs, YouTube videos, audio recordings, web articles, and image albums with per-chapter coverage bars ([Multimodal Hub](/en/sources/hub_multimodal/)).
- **Note Types** (<kbd>Alt+8</kbd>): customize Front/Back and Cloze note types, Jinja2 templates, and CSS styling ([Note Types & Templates](/en/cards/note-types-and-templates/)).

### AI Lab
- **Agent Editor** (<kbd>Alt+9</kbd>): create, prompt with Jinja2, assign tools, and version custom personas ([Agent Editor & A/B Testing](/en/ai-setup/agents-et-tests-ab/)).
- **Pipelines**: build and run multi-step DAG workflows powered by local RAG ([DAG & RAG Pipelines](/en/cards/dag_et_rag/)).
- **A/B Tests**: compare engines, prompts, or pipelines side-by-side on your own course excerpts ([Agent Editor & A/B Testing](/en/ai-setup/agents-et-tests-ab/)).

## 2. Top Bar & Sidebar Footer

In the **top bar** of the window:
- **Sidebar collapse toggle** and active view **breadcrumb**.
- **Search / Command Palette (<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>⌘K</kbd>)**: type a few letters to jump to a view, trigger an [`.apkg` export](/en/anki-sync/export-apkg/), open a guide, or change a setting without leaving the keyboard ([Keyboard Shortcuts](/en/guides/raccourcis_clavier/)).
- **AI Cost Counter (`Dépenses : 0.00 $ (0 tk)`)**: real-time cumulative spend and token usage across AI requests ([AI Providers & Budget](/en/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/)).
- **Quick Action Buttons**: **Import Anki Package** (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd>), **Export Anki Cards** (<kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd>), **Notifications** (alerts & diagnostics), and the **`✨ Mise à jour`** badge when an update is ready.

At the bottom of the **left sidebar**:
- **Help & Feedback**: quick access to documentation, troubleshooting ([FAQ & Troubleshooting](/en/guides/faq_depannage/)), and issue reporting.
- **Settings (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>)**: configure appearance, [AI Engines](/en/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/), [MCP](/en/ai-setup/consultant_mcp/) server, Anki, TTS, and shortcuts.
- **Profile Switcher (`Profil : <name>`)** and **MCP status indicator**: switch between isolated study workspaces in one click ([Profiles & Workspaces](/en/getting-started/profiles-and-workspaces/)).

## 3. Customizing Layouts and Themes

In **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) › **General**:
- Pick from **4 interchangeable layouts** (*Concept IDE*, *Concept macOS*, *Concept Dashboard*, *Concept Glassmorphism*) using the thumbnail grid.
- Choose **Appearance Mode** (*Dark*, *Light*, *Follow system theme*) independently from **12 bivalent Theme Families** (**24 built-in light/dark palettes**, plus JSON theme import/export).

# [EN] Managing Profiles and Your Collection
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/profiles-and-workspaces/
Description: Create isolated study profiles in AnkiDraft, manage per-profile SQLite databases and media folders, and protect your local data with backups.

AnkiDraft lets you completely isolate multiple collections using **user profiles**.

## 1. Why Use Multiple Profiles?

Each profile has its own SQLite database (`ankidraft.db`), `media/` folder, `staging/` area, and `backups/` snapshots. This makes profiles ideal for **splitting your work into large, focused collections**:
- **Separate your personal notes from your academic years** (e.g., *Personal Notes / Languages*, *Year 1 Med School*, *Year 2 Med School*, *Exam Prep*).
- **Avoid getting lost in bulky documents**: imported study materials (PDF textbooks, lecture slides, video transcripts) can quickly become quite large. Isolating each major area in its own profile keeps your library clean, fast, and easy to navigate.

## 2. Creating, Transferring, or Switching Profiles

1. Click **`Profil : <name>`** at the bottom of the left sidebar (or use the startup *Workspaces & Profiles* dialog).
2. Enter a clear name and click **+ Create** to add a new independent space, or select an existing profile to switch.
3. AnkiDraft automatically locks the active profile (`ProfileLockService`) to prevent concurrent write conflicts across windows.
4. Click **Transfer...** to selectively copy decks, tags, note types, or image albums from another profile into the active one, or **Delete this space** to remove an unused unlocked profile.

## 3. Automatic Backups

AnkiDraft automatically saves timestamped SQLite snapshots inside the profile's `backups/` subfolder (retaining up to 5 recent backups on startup as well as creating a safety snapshot before sensitive actions like replacing your collection from a `.colpkg` archive).

---

# [EN] Quickstart Guide
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/quickstart/
Description: Create, review, and export your first Anki flashcard deck in 5 minutes with AnkiDraft, and pick the step-by-step workflow tailored to your subject.

This guide walks you through creating your first Anki flashcard deck in minutes and helps you pick the end-to-end workflow that matches your study material and AI setup.

## Which workflow fits your goal?

Pick the step-by-step guide that matches your study material:

1. **[Written Docs & STEM: PDFs, formulas, and diagrams](/en/workflows/medecine-sciences-pdf/)** — pick the relevant chapters from a textbook, keep equations and figures, and check that every card is clear.
2. **[Languages & Pronunciation: vocabulary and offline audio](/en/workflows/langues-et-audio-tts/)** — add natural offline voice pronunciation to your vocabulary cards and fix ambiguous wording.
3. **[Video & Audio: YouTube lectures and recordings](/en/workflows/cours-video-youtube-audio/)** — transcribe recorded lectures and turn key explanations into flashcards.
4. **[Collection Cleanup & Hygiene for an existing Anki deck](/en/workflows/sauvetage-et-hygiene-anki-mcp/)** — import an `.apkg` deck or `.colpkg` collection, remove duplicates, split overly long cards, and export back without losing your review progress.
5. **[Fill knowledge gaps against a textbook](/en/cards/dag_et_rag/)** — link existing cards to textbook chapters to spot missed concepts right away.

- **[Cross-cutting mode — Work with zero API key using Claude or Cursor](/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/)** — applies to any of the workflows above if you prefer driving AnkiDraft from your existing AI plan.

## Two Ways to Work with AI

AnkiDraft works both on its own and connected to your existing AI assistant (Claude, Cursor).

| Dimension | Built-in Studio (inside the app) | With Your AI Assistant (Claude, Cursor) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **What you need** | Free offline model ([Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/)) or an [API key](/en/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/) | Your existing plan (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor) — **zero API key** |
| **How it works** | Visual buttons, chapter selection, and batch generation | Chat naturally in your AI assistant connected to AnkiDraft |
| **Best suited for** | Extracting PDF chapters, adding voice audio, editing formulas | Spotting gaps across decks, bulk cleanup, and card rewrites |
| **Your control** | Review every card before saving | **Approval required**: nothing changes until you click **Apply** |

## How to Get a Free API Key (Student Guide)

You do not need a credit card or paid subscription to use the built-in Studio — here are the easiest ways to get a free API key that works right inside AnkiDraft:

1. **Google AI Studio (`Gemini`) — easiest starting point**: sign in with a Google account at [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com/) and click **Create API key** (no credit card required). Paste the key (`AIzaSy...`) under **Settings > AI Engines > Gemini**, click **Test**, and pick the built-in **`Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite`** preset (great for PDFs and diagrams within daily rate limits; avoid sending sensitive private data on the free tier).
2. **OpenRouter (`:free`) — multiple free models from one key**: create a free account at [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/) with no credit card, generate a key (`sk-or-...`), and use built-in `$0` models ending in `:free` such as **`OpenRouter Free (Qwen 3.8 27B)`** (subject to per-minute and daily rate caps).
3. **Groq Console — ultra-fast open models**: generate a free key (`gsk_...`) at [console.groq.com](https://console.groq.com/) with no credit card for high-speed card drafting and auditing (subject to tokens-per-minute limits).
4. **Student perks, gateway & campus access**: use your university email to check eligibility for the **GitHub Student Developer Pack** (**GitHub Models**), **Google AI student offers**, **Mistral** ([console.mistral.ai](https://console.mistral.ai/)), the **OpenCode Gateway**, or university-hosted endpoints (added via **Add a model ▾ › Custom model…**).

:::tip
See exact UI presets, privacy tips, and token caps in [Configuring AI Providers](/en/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/).
:::

## Get Started in 4 Simple Steps

### Step 1: Select or Create Your Profile

On first launch, AnkiDraft opens the `default` profile. To keep bulky course files separate from personal decks, create a dedicated profile from **`Profil : default`** at the bottom of the left sidebar ([Manage profiles](/en/getting-started/profiles-and-workspaces/)).

### Step 2: Choose an AI Engine (Optional)

Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) and switch to **AI Engines**:
- **Free & 100% offline**: install [Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/) locally and pick a model.
- **With an API key (free or paid)**: paste a [free-tier key from the options above](#how-to-get-a-free-api-key-student-guide) (Google Gemini, OpenRouter `:free`, Groq…) or a paid OpenAI / Anthropic key, stored encrypted in your OS keychain.
- **Zero API key**: turn on the local connection in **MCP Server & Agents** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>) to use your [Claude or Cursor plan](/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/).

### Step 3: Import Your First Study Material

1. Open **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>) from the sidebar.
2. Drag and drop a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, or EPUB file, or paste a YouTube video link.
3. For a focused excerpt or free-form note, switch to **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>); to split and queue an entire textbook by chapter, open **Batch Factory** (<kbd>Alt+6</kbd>) › **Batch Slice Composer**.

### Step 4: Review, Improve, and Export to Anki

Review the generated cards, run a quick check in **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>) to catch overly long or vague cards, then press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> (**Export Anki Cards (.apkg)**). Double-click the exported `.apkg` file to add your cards directly into Anki.

> Want plain-language definitions with concrete Before / After examples? Read the [User Glossary](/en/guides/glossaire/).

# [EN] Visual Guide to the Distributed Lifecycle (AnkiDraft & Anki)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/
Description: Understand how the AnkiDraft authoring studio and the Anki spaced-repetition engine work together via .apkg and .colpkg without sync conflicts.

Welcome to the distributed workflow guide for AnkiDraft (formerly AnkiForge).

AnkiDraft and Anki work hand in hand as complementary tools:
- **AnkiDraft is your Authoring Studio**: your AI-assisted workspace where you organize textbooks, track chapter coverage (Smart Coverage / Cycle Global Distribué), design flashcards, and validate card quality.
- **Anki is your Spaced Repetition Engine (SRS)**: the application dedicated to your daily reviews. Anki holds exclusive authority over your review intervals, due dates, and spaced repetition algorithms (FSRS or SM-2).

Thanks to this strict boundary (**Sanctuarisation**), **you never risk losing your review progress in Anki or overwriting your study documents and AI models in AnkiDraft**.

---

## 1. The Global Workflow Cycle

The diagram below illustrates the workflow between creating cards in AnkiDraft and reviewing them in Anki:

1. **AnkiDraft Studio**: Import your study sources (PDF, articles, videos, audio lectures). The studio segments the text and tracks your chapter coverage.
2. **Staging Review**: Every generated flashcard goes through human validation and receives a permanent unique identifier (GUID).
3. **Export to Anki (.apkg)**: Export your new cards as an `.apkg` package and open it in Anki.
4. **Periodic Refresh (.colpkg)**: Review daily in Anki. Periodically export your `.colpkg` collection from Anki and drop it into AnkiDraft to refresh your retention statistics and sync card deletions.

---

## 2. Data Boundary: Studio Scope vs. Anki Scope (Sanctuarisation)

### 🛡️ Studio Scope (Strictly Preserved)
Never overwritten when you import an Anki collection:
- Original documents (PDFs, transcripts, Markdown files, image plates).
- Local semantic indexes and coverage links.
- AI personas, prompts, and generation pipelines.
- Application settings, themes, and custom shortcuts.

### 🗂️ Anki Collection Scope (Synchronized & Replaced)
Reflects your exact Anki collection:
- Decks and hierarchical sub-decks.
- Note types, Front/Back templates, and CSS styles.
- Notes, physical cards, flags, and SRS review counters.

---

## 3. Which Archive Format Should You Choose: .apkg or .colpkg?

| Criterion | Deck Package (`.apkg`) | Collection Archive (`.colpkg`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Purpose** | Share or add new/updated flashcards | Full replacement for exact alignment with Anki |
| **Behavior** | **Incremental merge**: adds or updates cards without touching other decks | **Full Anki scope replacement**: matches your Anki collection state |
| **Deletions** | Never deletes existing local cards | **Purges cards deleted in Anki (prevents Zombies)** |
| **Safety** | Smart Merge conflict dialog | **Automatic SQLite backup created before replacement** |

---

## 4. Typical Study Session Timeline

---

## 5. Preventing Zombie Cards (Zombies) and Empty Fronts

### 🧟 1. Eradicating Zombie Cards (Zombies)
When you delete an obsolete card in Anki and later import a `.colpkg` archive into AnkiDraft, the deleted card is permanently removed from AnkiDraft so it never reappears in future exports.

### 📄 2. Official Anki Non-Empty Front Rule
AnkiDraft evaluates conditional templates (`{{#Field}}...{{/Field}}` and `{{^Field}}...{{/Field}}`): if the rendered front of a card is empty, no physical card is created.

---

# [EN] FAQ and Troubleshooting
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/faq_depannage/
Description: Find answers to frequently asked questions and step-by-step troubleshooting for AnkiDraft installation, Ollama, PDF OCR, and Anki .apkg exports.

Find answers to the most common questions about AnkiDraft.

## 1. General Questions

### Does AnkiDraft replace Anki?
No—AnkiDraft and Anki complement each other. **AnkiDraft** is the authoring and quality-auditing studio where you turn textbooks and lectures into atomic flashcards, while **Anki** (Desktop, AnkiWeb, AnkiMobile, AnkiDroid) is the spaced-repetition engine where you do your daily reviews.

### Can I use AnkiDraft for free and offline?
Yes. AnkiDraft is free, runs offline on your computer, and supports free local AI models via [Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/) without any paid API subscription.

### Are my PDFs and flashcards uploaded to the cloud?
No. Your PDFs, SQLite database, and media files stay locally on your drive (`~/.ankidraft/`). If you configure a cloud AI provider (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude), only the text passages you explicitly select for card generation are sent directly to your API account.

## 2. Troubleshooting

### macOS shows a security prompt on first launch
Make sure you dragged **AnkiDraft** into your **Applications** folder from the `.dmg` disk image. If macOS asks for confirmation on first open, right-click the **AnkiDraft** icon and select **Open**.

### My math formulas do not render in Anki
Verify that your equations use standard MathJax/KaTeX delimiters (`\( ... \)` for inline math and `\[ ... \]` for centered block equations).

### How do I report a bug or request a feature?
Inside AnkiDraft, open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Help** > **Report an Idea or Bug**, or open an issue on the [official GitHub repository](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/issues).

---

# [EN] User Glossary: Key AnkiDraft Concepts Explained Simply
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/glossaire/
Description: Understand every core AnkiDraft concept (Wozniak rules, Cloze, Smart Coverage, DAG, RAG, MCP, Safeguard) with clear Before / After study examples.

AnkiDraft combines spaced-repetition best practices with local AI tools. This glossary explains every technical term in plain English, paired with a concrete **Before / After** example.

---

## 1. Atomic Knowledge & Wozniak's 20 Rules

A core principle from Piotr Wozniak (creator of SuperMemo): a great flashcard tests **one short, unambiguous fact** at a time (minimum information principle). AnkiDraft's linter automatically spots bloated or vague prompts.

- **Before**: *Front:* "Explain the Krebs cycle (steps, rate-limiting enzymes, ATP/NADH/FADH2 yield)." ➔ Too dense to grade honestly during reviews.
- **After**: 3 crisp, independent cards: (1) "Which enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting step of the Krebs cycle?", (2) "How many NADH molecules are produced per turn of the Krebs cycle?", (3) "Where in the cell does the Krebs cycle take place?".

---

## 2. Cloze Deletion

A fill-in-the-blank card (`{{c1::hidden term}}`) that hides one key word or phrase inside a clear sentence so you recall it directly in context (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd>).

- **Before**: "Define osmosis?" / "Movement of solvent across a semipermeable membrane from lower to higher solute concentration."
- **After**: "During osmosis, solvent moves across a semipermeable membrane from a {{c1::hypotonic (lower solute)}} solution to a {{c2::hypertonic (higher solute)}} solution."

---

## 3. Smart Coverage

A traceability tracker linking each generated card back to its exact source heading or page. It shows which chapters of your PDF already have flashcards and which sections are still uncovered.

- **Before**: Manually flipping through a 180-page textbook wondering whether you forgot subsection 3.4.
- **After**: The *Smart Coverage* gauge reports `Chapter 3: 82% covered — Section 3.4 (0 cards)` and lets you draft cards solely for that gap.

---

## 4. Scoping: Exclude vs. Neutralize

Two non-destructive actions to filter a textbook without deleting pages ([Scope & Chapters](/en/sources/scope-and-slices/)):
- **Exclude**: temporarily hides an off-syllabus chapter from AI generation.
- **Neutralize**: removes structural boilerplate (cover, table of contents, acknowledgments) from the *Smart Coverage* denominator.

- **Before**: A 300-page book with 30 pages of index and bibliography caps your coverage at 90% or generates useless cards about publisher copyrights.
- **After**: Index neutralized, bibliography excluded ➔ coverage accurately reaches **100% of active chapters** with zero junk cards.

---

## 5. Generation Pipeline (DAG)

An automated multi-step workflow (e.g., retrieve key passages ➔ synthesize clean Markdown ➔ draft cards ➔ add TTS audio ➔ stage for human review).

- **Before**: Copying a chapter into a chat box, generating cards, fixing broken LaTeX manually, then creating audio one card at a time.
- **After**: Clicking **Run Pipeline** executes the full workflow automatically and delivers clean drafts ready to review.

---

## 6. Local Semantic Search (RAG)

100% local indexing on your computer that lets AI retrieve relevant sections of your textbooks by **meaning** (not just exact keywords) before drafting or auditing cards.

- **Before**: Stuffing an entire textbook into a prompt (slow, expensive, and prone to hallucinations).
- **After**: Local RAG pulls only the 3 paragraphs relevant to the concept and keeps exact page provenance.

---

## 7. MCP Server (Model Context Protocol)

An open standard built into AnkiDraft that lets your external AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity) read your courses and decks locally with zero extra API keys.

- **Before**: Copy-pasting notes back and forth between Anki, PDFs, and a browser chat window.
- **After**: Asking Claude directly *"Audit my Cardiology deck and draft missing cards for Chapter 4"* queries AnkiDraft live.

---

## 8. Safeguard & Staged Bundle (Two-Phase Human Approval)

A mandatory safety buffer: no AI proposal (create, edit, split, or delete) ever modifies your database directly. Every change enters a **Staged Bundle** with a Before / After diff until you click **Apply**.

- **Before**: Worrying that an automated prompt or script might accidentally overwrite 200 cards.
- **After**: You inspect every proposed card change side-by-side in the Safeguard and stay in 100% control.

---

## 9. Domain Gap Diagnosis & the 3 Cognitive Pathologies

A neuro-symbolic audit (`diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`) scanning all your decks together against a study topic to catch 3 pathologies:
- **Type 1 (Missing concepts)**: textbook concepts with zero matching flashcards.
- **Type 2 (Non-atomicity)**: bloated multi-fact cards needing splitting.
- **Type 3 (Bilingual glue)**: two languages mixed awkwardly in one card or bare word translations lacking context.

- **Before**: Realizing right before finals that 3 core topics are missing or scattered across unrelated decks.
- **After**: The audit collects related orphan cards across decks and pinpoints exact gaps and splits needed.

---

## 10. Studio Scope vs. Anki Collection Scope (`.apkg` vs. `.colpkg`)

AnkiDraft isolates authoring assets (**Studio Scope**: PDFs, transcripts, RAG indexes, prompts) from synced cards (**Anki Collection Scope**).
- `.apkg`: adds or merges a targeted deck.
- `.colpkg`: mirrors your complete Anki collection (removes cards deleted in Anki while keeping all PDFs intact).

- **Before**: Importing a full Anki backup risked wiping study notes or resurrecting deleted cards ("zombie cards").
- **After**: `.colpkg` sync updates your collection cleanly while keeping Studio sources safe and preventing zombie cards ([Distributed Lifecycle Guide](/en/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/)).

---

## 11. Smart Merge

A 3-way visual diff (**Local**, **Common Base**, **Incoming**) inspired by developer merge tools: when importing an updated `.apkg` from a classmate, only true text conflicts require your decision.

- **Before**: Blindly overwriting your personal edits or losing a teammate's additions when importing a shared deck.
- **After**: Pick the exact version per field while preserving media and review scheduling.

---

## 12. Leech Card

Anki's term for a card you repeatedly fail during reviews—almost always because it is too verbose, poorly phrased, or interferes with a sibling card.

- **Before**: Seeing the same frustrating card fail 8 times a month without sticking.
- **After**: AnkiDraft spots leeches from synced lapse counters and suggests splitting or clarifying them with distinctive cues.

---

# [EN] Keyboard Shortcuts Reference
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/raccourcis_clavier/
Description: Official reference of all keyboard shortcuts in AnkiDraft by category and scope to navigate workspaces, edit cards, and run AI pipelines fast.

This page lists the default keyboard shortcuts in AnkiDraft. You can customize any shortcut in **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Keyboard**.

> On macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> maps automatically to <kbd>Cmd ⌘</kbd>.

## 1. Global Application Actions

| Action | Default Shortcut | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Command Palette** | <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> | `Application` | Open the global command palette omnibox |
| **Settings** | <kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd> | `Application` | Open the Settings dialog |
| **Save** | <kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd> | `Application` | Save changes in the active view |
| **Run Primary Action** | <kbd>Ctrl+Return</kbd> | `Application` | Trigger the main action in the active view (generate, run) |
| **Find / Search** | <kbd>Ctrl+F</kbd> | `Application` | Focus the search field in the active view |
| **Import Anki Package (.apkg / .colpkg)** | <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> | `Application` | Open the collection or deck import wizard |
| **Export Anki Cards (.apkg)** | <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> | `Application` | Open the `.apkg` card export dialog |
| **Interactive Guided Tour** | <kbd>F1</kbd> | `Application` | Launch the interactive feature tour |

## 2. Workspace Navigation

| Action | Default Shortcut | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dashboard** | <kbd>Ctrl+1</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Dashboard view |
| **Editor & Browser** | <kbd>Ctrl+2</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Note Editor and Card Browser |
| **Documents & Sources** | <kbd>Ctrl+3</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Document Hub |
| **Generation & Pipelines** | <kbd>Ctrl+4</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to Batch AI Generation |
| **Quality & Wozniak Audit** | <kbd>Ctrl+5</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Wozniak Quality Linter |
| **AI Consultant** | <kbd>Ctrl+6</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the interactive AI Consultant |

## 3. Note Editor & Formatting

| Action | Default Shortcut | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **New Note** | <kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd> | `View` | Create a new flashcard note |
| **Duplicate Note** | <kbd>Ctrl+D</kbd> | `View` | Duplicate the selected note |
| **Delete Note** | <kbd>Delete</kbd> | `View` | Delete the selected note(s) |
| **Bold** | <kbd>Ctrl+B</kbd> | `Widget` | Toggle bold text formatting |
| **Italic** | <kbd>Ctrl+I</kbd> | `Widget` | Toggle italic text formatting |
| **Underline** | <kbd>Ctrl+U</kbd> | `Widget` | Toggle underline formatting |
| **Insert Cloze Deletion** | <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd> | `Widget` | Wrap selection in `{{c1::...}}` |
| **Undo / Redo** | <kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+Z</kbd> | `Widget` | Undo or redo the last edit |

# [EN] Image Albums, Photo Scans, and Vision OCR
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/albums-images/
Description: Combine whiteboard photos, scanned handouts, and diagrams in an Image Album, transcribe pages with Vision AI, index in RAG, and forge flashcards.

Took photos of the lecture whiteboard, snapped handwritten study sheets, or collected loose anatomy plates? In **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>), **Image Albums** keep your visuals organized page by page so you can clean, transcribe with Vision AI, and turn them into flashcards.

## 1. Creating and Organizing an Image Album

1. Open **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>) and click **Create an Image Album** (or **Create album** on the empty view).
2. Enter a title, select a target folder, and pick the initial sort order:
   - **Natural alphanumeric sort** (`page_1`, `page_2`…)
   - **EXIF capture date** (camera chronological order)
   - **Raw import order**
3. Inside the album viewer, each plate includes quick actions: reorder left/right, **rotate 90°**, **inspect / crop**, delete, or append new files (**Add images**).

## 2. Transcribing the Album with Vision AI

1. Click **Transcribe album…** in the album toolbar.
2. Select a **multimodal Vision-capable engine** (such as `Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite` or a local Ollama vision model; AnkiDraft warns when a selected engine cannot read images).
3. Target the exact plates to process:
   - **Entire album**
   - **Untranscribed plates only**
   - **Stale plates** (modified or rotated since the last OCR pass)
   - **Custom range** (e.g., `1-5, 8, 12-15`)
4. Pick the **Image data type** and optional formatting guidance. If any page hits a network or quota limit, use **Retry failures** instead of re-running the whole album.

## 3. Visual RAG, PDF Compilation, and Flashcards

- **Visual RAG**: indexes your plates and diagrams in FAISS for multimodal semantic search.
- **Compile to PDF**: merges all album pages (preserving rotations and crops) into a single readable PDF.
- **Forge Cards**: opens the album directly in **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>), or launch **Image Occlusion** from the inspector to mask diagram labels.

:::tip
Using Claude Code, Cursor, or Antigravity with zero API key? The `ingestion-albums-visuels` Skill in `~/ankiforge_agentique` can transcribe and structure album plates before staging flashcards in **Safeguard & Validation** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>).
:::

---

# [EN] Document Hub and Multimodal Formats
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/hub_multimodal/
Description: Overview of supported sources in AnkiDraft — PDF, Web, YouTube, audio, DOCX, PPTX, EPUB, notebooks, code, and Image Albums with full source tracing.

The **My Documents** view (`<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>`) centralizes all your study materials in one place, lets you organize them into folders (via drag-and-drop), import documents from another profile, and preserves a direct link between every flashcard and its exact source passage.

## 1. Supported Study Sources

| Source Type | Formats | What AnkiDraft Extracts |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **PDF Textbooks & Handouts** | `.pdf` | Chapter outline, text, tables, figures, and LaTeX math (PyMuPDF / pypdf, or Marker OCR on demand) |
| **Image Albums & Scans** | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.bmp`, `.tiff`, `.gif` | Visual spreads, Vision AI transcription, and visual RAG — [see dedicated guide](/en/sources/albums-images/) |
| **Online Videos** | YouTube URLs | Timestamped subtitles, or audio transcription (`yt-dlp` + Whisper) |
| **Audio Recordings** | `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.m4a`, `.ogg`, `.flac`, `.aac`, `.wma`, `.webm` | Paragraph-segmented transcript (local Whisper or OpenAI/Groq API) + built-in player |
| **Web Articles & Wikipedia** | `http://`, `https://` | Clean article body (multi-page merge, MathML → LaTeX, SPA JavaScript rendering) |
| **Office, Ebooks & Text** | `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.epub`, `.md`, `.txt` | Heading hierarchy, lists, tables, and slide speaker notes |
| **Notebooks & Source Code** | `.ipynb`, `.py` | Code cells, markdown explanations, docstrings, and structured blocks |

## 2. Jump Back to the Source in One Click

While reviewing or editing any flashcard in the editor, click **View Course ➔** (`DocumentSourceBadge`) to jump straight back to the corresponding chapter and paragraph in **My Documents**. From the **Coverage** inspector tab, you can also click **Synchronize Cards** to refresh source-to-card coverage alignment.
